content_html:
Cusco is a fascinating destination with a wide variety of attractions, from archaeological sites to cultural and natural experiences. Depending on the time you have available, here we leave you recommended itineraries for 3, 5 and 7 days in the imperial city.

Cusco in 3 Days: The Essentials

If you have only three days, you must prioritize the must-sees of the city and its surroundings.

Day 1: Exploration in the City of Cusco

Plaza de Armas and the Cathedral of Cusco.

Coricancha, the Temple of the Sun.

Sacsayhuamán and its impressive Inca architecture.

San Blas neighborhood and its vibrant artistic life.

Day 2: Sacred Valley of the Incas

Pisac and its artisan market.

Ollantaytambo Fortress.

Train trip to Aguas Calientes.

Day 3: Machu Picchu

Dawn in the Inca citadel.

Guided tour of Machu Picchu.

Return to Cusco by train.

Cusco in 5 Days: More Adventure

If you have five days, you can explore more natural and archaeological destinations.

Day 4: Mountain of Seven Colors (Vinicunca) or Palccoyo

Excursion to Vinicunca or Palccoyo.

Walk through the Andean landscapes.

Return to Cusco in the afternoon.

Day 5: Maras and Moray

Visit to the circular terraces of Moray.

Discovery of the Maras Salt Mines.

Lunch in Urubamba and return to Cusco.

Cusco in 7 Days: Complete Experience

If you have one week, you can immerse yourself even more in the culture, history and nature of Cusco.

Day 6: Trekking in the Sacred Valley or Humantay Lagoon

Hike to Humantay Lagoon or explore less crowded routes in the Sacred Valley.

Connection with nature and impressive landscapes.

Day 7: Free Day and Gastronomic Experience

Enjoy a relaxing day exploring the San Pedro Market.

Try local cuisine in typical food restaurants. Tour of museums and souvenir shopping.

Conclusion

Whether you visit Cusco for 3, 5 or 7 days, there are incredible experiences waiting for you. Plan your time well and enjoy the magic of this unique city in the Andes.
